subject: Streaming chat latency recovery summary and immediate client runbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lim <sophie.lim@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming chat latency recovery summary and immediate client runbook

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for working with us while we triaged the spike this morning. I wanted to send a concise summary of what happened, the immediate mitigations we’ve applied for BrightBridge, and suggested changes you can make on your side to reduce user-visible impact while we finish the full postmortem.

What happened (brief):
- Between 07:05 and 07:42 PT we observed a sustained rise in token emission latency on our US real-time pool serving the streaming/chat endpoint used by BrightBridge (route: /v1/realtime/generate).
- Root cause (short): a coordination bug in KV cache eviction combined with a model kernel fallback path that caused increased per-token compute for a subset of long-session requests.

Actions we’ve taken (already applied):
- Rolled a targeted fix to the KV cache eviction heuristic to stop repeated cache thrashing.
- Temporarily routed BrightBridge traffic to a warmed-capacity shard with conservative kernel selection (trade: slightly higher token compute cost, lower variance).
- Applied a short-term throttle rule to cap streaming burst-window at 300 requests/min for your API key to avoid repeated retries.

Immediate mitigations for BrightBridge (recommended client changes):
1) Switch to chunked streaming: If you’re using long single-request messages, split them into multiple shorter messages; this reduces peak KV growth.
2) Reduce max_tokens per generation to 512 for interactive flows until we’ve verified stability.
3) Implement optimistic local buffering (200–350 ms) and client-side exponential backoff on 502/503 with jitter.
4) Configure an automated fallback to a lower-capacity model family (e.g., redwood-medium) for non-critical sessions during peak windows.

We’ve attached a short runbook with example curl/SDK snippets (client_runbook_v1.pdf) and a set of diagnostic logs we collected (latency-diagnostics-20260915.tar.gz).

Next steps:
- We’d like to run a 30-min postmortem call tomorrow to review the detailed timeline and mitigation timeline. I’ve tentatively proposed 09:00 PT — does that work for you?
- We will follow up with a formal postmortem doc and an SLA credit proposal (we’re already preparing an initial credit form).

Apologies for the disruption — our priority is to make sure your production experience is stable. Please let me know if you need us to enable any of the client-side mitigations for you via config, and whether 09:00 PT tomorrow works.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BrightBridge follow-up and suggested temporary configs

Folks — quick coordinator note after Sophie’s reply:

1) Warmed shard: we can keep BrightBridge assigned to the warmed shard for 24 hours as Karthik requested; Connor will own scaling until 09/16 09:00 PT.
2) Client-runbook snippets: I’ve drafted conservative SDK examples for chunked streaming and model fallback. Key items to share with BrightBridge now:
   - SDK example: set max_tokens=512, streaming_chunk_size=512, enable_chunked=true
   - Fallback policy: if latency > 800ms for three consecutive tokens, switch to redwood-medium and continue the session with a short system prompt noting the model change.
   - Retry/backoff: base_delay=250ms, factor=1.6, max_delay=2000ms, jitter=0.25
3) SLA credit: recommend offering a one-time credit equal to 10% of last month’s line-item usage for the impacted service window and an expedited engineering review. Laura — can you prepare the SLA credit form and approval routing?
4) Postmortem owner: Mina will lead the internal write-up; Karthik to own customer communications.

I’ll attach the SDK snippets to the internal ticket and share a short set of curl commands for their eng team.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
